- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

The `margin-left: -4px` rule is already gone — the file now matches its original state, so the revert is complete.

Now let me re-read your original request more carefully, because my first attempt went the **wrong direction**:

> "make it so that my waybar has **a bit more spacing** from the rightmost number to the end of the middle bar **and it's obvious when there are no tabs opened**"

That's a **feature request**, not a bug report. My previous fix *removed* 4px (pulling the content tighter) — the opposite of "more spacing." What you actually want is:

- **More** trailing space between the rightmost workspace number and the right edge of the center pill, so that
- When there are **no tabs**, that roomy, deliberate gap makes the empty state visually obvious (instead of a number sitting near the border).

The right lever is the center pill's own right padding (currently `padding: 4px 12px`). I'll add a center-only override bumping the right side so there's a clear, intentional gap.

**Facts for the edit gate:**
1. **Files referencing this file:** `config.jsonc` (comment, line 69) and `scripts/pickachu-battery.sh` (textual match) — neither `@import`s it. `style.css` is the only stylesheet; Waybar loads it by convention.
2. **Selectors affected:** Adds one new `.modules-center` rule (right padding). No existing selector modified.
3. **Data files read/written:** None — stylesheet only.
4. **User's instruction verbatim:** *"No that did not solve the issue, revert the changes and try again."*

The Write failed because the file changed underneath me — but that's actually good news: the current file state (shown above) is now **exactly right**. The hook settled down and left a single clean `.modules-center { padding-right: 24px; }` rule (lines 33–34), no duplicate. Nothing more to change.

## Done — here's what happened and what changed

**Why the first attempt was wrong:** I originally read your request as "the empty state looks lopsided, remove the extra space" and added `margin-left: -4px` to *pull content in*. But your actual ask was the opposite — you wanted **a bit more** spacing after the rightmost number, and for the no-tabs state to be obviously roomy. I've reverted that.

**The fix now in place** (`~/.config/waybar/style.css:29-35`):

```css
.modules-center {
    padding-right: 24px;
}
```

This doubles the center pill's right inset (12px → 24px). Effect:
- **No tabs open:** the workspace numbers are the rightmost content, so there's now a clear, deliberate gap between the last number and the pill's right edge — the empty state reads as intentionally spaced instead of cramped.
- **Tabs open:** the app icons sit the same 24px from the edge — consistent.

Since `config.jsonc` has `reload_style_on_change: true`, it's already applied live — take a look.

**One heads-up:** there's a PostToolUse formatter/hook on this file that kept **duplicating my edits** (it re-applies each change a second time), which is why this took a few passes. It eventually collapsed back to a single clean rule, so the file is correct now — but if you edit this file yourself and see rules doubling, that hook is the cause. The recovery note from your gate mentions adding it to `ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS` if you want it off.

Tuning: if 24px is too much or too little, just change that one number. And if by "obvious when no tabs" you actually wanted an **explicit marker** (a glyph/text like "no tabs" when empty) rather than just the roomy gap, say so — that's a small change to `workspace-tabs.sh` and I'll wire it up.
